about: What Shree-Lipi's own composers write for Unicode Bangla / Assamese (S8BanU64.dll and S8Ban764.dll, Shree-Lipi nxt, typed the same keys into both). Each row: the Unicode string, the preferred bytes (hex, one byte per glyph code) and, when there are any, the other spellings the composer also accepts. The bytes are the composer's, in the codes the SHREE-BAN 4/5/6 fonts (SHREE-BAN-*) draw them with: the composer writes ব and ৰ as AF and ৱ as A4, which in every SHREE-BAN font draw ব্ল and ব, so here ব is A4 (the code the composer itself uses for ব inside ব্ব and ব্ল), ৱ is 9E and ৰ is B9 (no SHREE-BAN font has ৰ; the SHREE-ASS fonts draw it at B9). Left out: 561 composer rows that lose a typed letter (ক্গু written as গু, ৱ written with the র glyph) - its bugs, not spellings. Changed, where the composer's spelling does not draw the text (tools/BanTruth/Decisions.cs): Assamese ৰ as reph or ra-phala (ৰ্ক, ক্ৰ) has the bytes of the same text with র - the composer writes ৰ there as a letter with a visible hasanta, its Assamese keyboards typing র for ra (and the 127 ৰ rows with no র twin in the capture: a ra-phala with a hasanta is the composer's own letter + visible hasanta + ra, ক্ৰ্র = 41 F4 A1 B9 F8; a reph takes the composer's bytes for the text typed in its own order); the filler FF of দ্গ দ্ঘ ধ্ব ব্ব ড়্গ ৱ্ৱ, which draws nothing (দগ, two letters), is the subscript ব AB for ধ্ব ব্ব and a visible hasanta for the others; a lone র্ is B9 F4, not the pending reph A2; ব্ঢ ব্ড চ্ঞ, which the composer writes 81 8D 90 - C1 control code points Word and RichEdit draw as nothing - are letter + visible hasanta + letter (ব্ঢ = A4 F4 6E A1); ড় ঢ় with ু ূ and ঁ or a reph, where the composer's spelling draws no ু ূ (ড়ুঁ = D8 6C A1 F2 A1, র্ড়ু = D8 6C A1 A2 A1), keep the sign the way the composer's own alternative does (র্ড়ু = D8 6C A2 A1 E6, ড়ুঁ = D8 6C F2 A1 E6). Every row that ends in a hasanta already has the visible halant F4 in the composer's own spelling. ৱ stays 9E here: the Bangla fonts hold it only at U+009E (drawn by nothing but the app's preview), so their tables pass ৱ through, reported; the Assamese fonts draw it at AF. The other font families (7: SHREE-BAN7-*, Shree-Ban7-001/002; Assamese: SHREE-ASS-*, SHREE-ASS7-*, Shree-Ass7-001/002) use the same spellings with a few codes moved; tools/BanTruth (Family.cs) and the tests say which. tools/BanTruth builds and checks the shree-ban7 / ban456 / ass7 / ass456 / ass7w tables against it.
